title: Unauthorized disclosure of camera/sensor data
description: Homeowner's camera and sensor data could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through the Home Hub or network, potentially exposing private home activities and personal information.
assumptions: Home Hub or network is compromised; data is transmitted without adequate encryption or access controls.

title: Linkability of device data to homeowner identity
description: Device enrollment and usage data could be linked to the Homeowner's identity, enabling profiling of their behavior, location patterns, and home routines.
assumptions: System logs or metadata contain identifiers that can be correlated with the homeowner's account.

title: Identification of homeowner from device data
description: Even if the homeowner attempts to remain anonymous, device data (e.g., camera feeds, sensor readings) could be used to identify them or infer their presence at home.
assumptions: Device data contains unique identifiers or patterns that can be traced back to the homeowner.

title: Usurpation of homeowner account access
description: An attacker could potentially gain unauthorized access to the Homeowner's account, allowing them to control cameras/sensors or access stored data.
assumptions: Account credentials are weakly protected; authentication mechanisms are vulnerable to attacks.

title: Access code disclosure during transmission
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest user at the Home Hub could be observed by bystanders (shoulder surfing, audio recording, or network interception), leading to unauthorized disclosure of the credential.
assumptions: Guest enters code in a public or semi-public space; code is transmitted in a way that could be intercepted.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Dd.1.1 is inferred from context; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Usurpation of guest access
description: An observer who witnesses the guest entering the access code could subsequently use that code to gain unauthorized access to the home, effectively usurping the guest's legitimate access.
assumptions: Access code is not sufficiently complex or is transmitted in a vulnerable manner; no additional authentication required.
uncertainty_note: Tree node U.1.2 is inferred from context; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Linkability of guest access events
description: The access event could be linked to other guest activities or to the specific guest identity, potentially revealing patterns of behavior or association with other system interactions.
assumptions: Access logs or system responses could be correlated with other data sources to identify the guest.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is inferred from context; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Linkability of Event Patterns
description: An attacker with access to the local event log could link multiple motion/door/sensor events together to reconstruct detailed patterns of household activity, including occupancy schedules, routine behaviors, and presence/absence patterns.
assumptions: The local event log is accessible to unauthorized parties or the attacker has physical access to the Home Hub/DS1.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node L.1.1 based on Process→DataStore mapping context.

title: Identification of Individuals from Event Data
description: Motion, door, and sensor events could be used to identify specific individuals or their presence in the home, potentially revealing who is present, when they enter/leave, and their movement patterns within the house.
assumptions: Event data contains sufficient detail (e.g., timestamps, sensor locations) that could be correlated with known individuals.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node I.1.1 based on Process→DataStore mapping context.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Event Log Contents
description: The local event log containing motion/door/sensor events could be accessed by unauthorized parties, leading to disclosure of sensitive information about household activities, occupancy patterns, and potentially security-related events.
assumptions: The local event log is not adequately protected from unauthorized access.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node D.1.1 based on Process→DataStore mapping context.

title: Data Manipulation of Event Log
description: An attacker with access to the local event log could alter, delete, or inject false events, compromising the integrity of the security monitoring system and potentially masking unauthorized access or creating false alarms.
assumptions: The local event log is not adequately protected from tampering.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node Dd.1.1 based on Process→DataStore mapping context.

title: Linkability of camera clips to other surveillance data
description: Uploaded camera clips could be linked to other surveillance data or user activity data, enabling correlation of movements and behaviors across different contexts.
assumptions: Cloud storage may contain or be accessible to other data sources that could be correlated with this footage.
uncertainty_note: Using L.1.1 as a reasonable node for linkability threats in Process->DataStore flows

title: Identifiability of individuals in camera footage
description: Camera clips inherently contain identifiable information about individuals, including faces, license plates, and personal activities, which could be used to identify and track specific persons.
assumptions: Camera footage captures identifiable human subjects and activities.
uncertainty_note: Using I.1.1 as a reasonable node for identifiability threats in Process->DataStore flows

title: Unauthorized disclosure of stored camera footage
description: Cloud video storage could be compromised, leading to unauthorized access to stored camera clips by malicious actors, resulting in privacy violations.
assumptions: Cloud storage systems are vulnerable to security breaches and unauthorized access.
uncertainty_note: Using D.1.1 as a reasonable node for disclosure threats at DataStore level

title: Usurpation during upload transmission
description: Camera clips could be intercepted during upload from Home Hub to cloud storage, allowing attackers to impersonate the legitimate uploader or access the data in transit.
assumptions: Upload transmission may not be fully encrypted or authenticated, creating interception opportunities.
uncertainty_note: Using U.1.1 as a reasonable node for usurpation threats in Process->DataStore flows

title: Excessive motion data disclosure to backend
description: Home Hub forwards real-time motion alert data to Mobile App Backend, potentially exposing personal data about occupancy patterns and routines beyond what's strictly necessary for the alert function.
assumptions: Motion data contains personal information (occupancy patterns, routines) and the transfer exceeds minimal data requirements.
uncertainty_note: Using Dd.4 from context [5] as it addresses excessive exposure to known parties; this is a reasonable fit for Process→Process data transfer.

title: Notification interception during transmission
description: Motion-detected notification could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission from backend to homeowner's device, revealing when and where the homeowner is present.
assumptions: Network transmission is not fully encrypted or authentication is weak
uncertainty_note: Assuming standard mobile app security practices apply

title: Excessive data in motion notification
description: Notification may contain more data than necessary (e.g., precise location, timestamp, motion type) when a simple alert would suffice, violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Notification includes detailed motion metadata beyond what's needed for homeowner awareness
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual notification payload design

title: Linkability of motion events to homeowner profile
description: Motion-detected notifications could be linked to other data about the homeowner's behavior patterns, location history, or daily routines, enabling profiling.
assumptions: Homeowner has other data sources that could be correlated with motion events
uncertainty_note: Depends on what other data the homeowner has access to

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with the cloud analytics vendor may be linkable with other data sources (e.g., user profiles, device identifiers) to re-identify individuals or create detailed user profiles.
assumptions: The vendor may have access to additional data sources that could be correlated with the shared analytics.
uncertainty_note: Using tree node L.1.1 based on Process→ExternalEntity mapping; aggregated data linkability is a recognized concern in analytics sharing.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure to Third Parties
description: The cloud analytics vendor may disclose the shared device-usage analytics to unauthorized third parties, including competitors, advertisers, or government entities, without proper authorization.
assumptions: The vendor's security controls may be inadequate, or contractual agreements may not sufficiently restrict data usage.
uncertainty_note: D.1.1 selected for Process→ExternalEntity flow; high severity due to external vendor's potential data misuse.

title: Regulatory Compliance Violation
description: Sharing aggregated device-usage analytics with an external cloud vendor may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) if proper consent, data minimization, or cross-border transfer requirements are not met.
assumptions: The data may contain quasi-identifiable information, and the vendor may be located in jurisdictions with different privacy standards.
uncertainty_note: Nc.1.1 selected for Process→ExternalEntity flow; regulatory compliance is critical for external data sharing.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video data during retrieval
description: The mobile app backend (P2) retrieves video data from the cloud storage (DS2) and may expose it to unauthorized parties through improper access controls, insecure transmission, or inadequate authentication during the retrieval process.
assumptions: The process P2 may not have proper access controls or encryption when handling the video data during retrieval.
uncertainty_note: Using generic D.1.1.1 node as specific tree node not provided in context

title: Video data may identify the homeowner
description: The video clip retrieved from cloud storage contains visual information that can identify the homeowner, creating identifiability risks when the video is processed or displayed by the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Video content inherently contains identifiable information about the homeowner.
uncertainty_note: Generic I.1.1.1 node used as specific tree node not provided in context

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: The mobile app backend (P2) may retain the retrieved video data longer than necessary for the playback purpose, violating the storage limitation principle of data protection.
assumptions: The process may cache or store the video beyond the immediate playback session.
uncertainty_note: Tree node Nc.1.1.4 from context applies to storage limitation principle
